chunks: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

The proof is upon the claimant, and the oath is upon the one against whom the claim is made. Reconciliation is permissible among the Muslims, except a reconciliation that makes a haram matter halal, or makes a halal matter haram.

key_terms.حَرَامًا: that which is forbidden by Allah
key_terms.حَلَالًا: that which is permitted by Allah
key_terms.ٱلصُّلْحُ: reconciliation or legal settlement between parties
key_terms.ٱلْبَيِّنَةُ: clear proof or evidentiary proof required from the claimant
key_terms.ٱلْمُدَّعَى عَلَيْهِ: the person against whom the claim is made
key_terms.ٱلْيَمِينُ: the oath sworn in response to a claim

ai.seo_question: What is the rule for proof, oaths, and reconciliation in Islamic legal disputes?
ai.summary: This hadith lays down a foundational principle of judicial procedure: the claimant must present proof, while the defendant responds with an oath. It also establishes that settlement and reconciliation are valid among Muslims so long as they do not violate the boundaries of halal and haram.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3267 - The Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) said:

"The burden of proof is upon the claimant, and the oath is upon the one who denies the claim.
Reconciliation is permissible among Muslims, except for a reconciliation that makes something unlawful (to be) lawful, or makes something lawful (to be) unlawful."
